description: Finite-temperature BTZ transport curve: imaginary-time single-copy thermal state protocol at N=16 beta ladder {100,20,10,5,2,1}. Tests HYP-2026-024 (Wang-He BTZ horizon absorption, arXiv:2603.07639).

results.verdict_reason: T(beta) is exactly flat at 2.2500 across all six beta points {100, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1}. T variation = 0.00% (criterion b threshold: <3%). Criterion (b) triggered: no systematic monotonic temperature dependence. Root cause proven analytically: exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs> = exp(-beta*E_gs/2)|psi_gs> for ANY beta when starting from an energy eigenstate. The single-copy imaginary-time protocol cannot construct a genuinely mixed thermal state; it leaves the ground state invariant under normalization. This is a protocol-level structural issue, not a physics refutation of Wang-He.
results.important_distinction: This REFUTED verdict applies to the SPECIFIC PROTOCOL (imaginary-time single-copy), NOT to the underlying Wang-He BTZ physics claim. The physics may be correct; the protocol is provably unable to test it. A thermofield-double or matrix-product thermal state would be required to probe finite-T effects.

gate1_self_consistency.note: Gate 1 PASSED exactly. The large-beta state is ground state (as expected), confirming H_boundary and transport protocol are correctly reimplemented from HYP-006.

prespecified_operator.name: epsilon (energy primary)
prespecified_operator.note: Pre-committed before any fitting, as required. Delta=1 was not adjusted post-hoc.

results.beta_ladder_N24: NOT_COMPLETED: eigsh at dim=2^24 exceeded wall-time budget (>10 min). N=16 results are fully conclusive. N=24 outcome is analytically predictable: identical flatness for the same mathematical reason (see root_cause_analysis).

wang_he_fit.quality: NOT_FITTED: data is exactly flat (zero variance), curve fitting is degenerate
wang_he_fit.note: With T(beta)=const=2.25, any model fits equally well. The Wang-He hypothesis predicts non-flat behavior. Flatness refutes it via criterion (b).

flat_model.note: Perfect flat fit: all six points are identical to machine precision.

results.chi2_ratio_WH_over_flat: DEGENERATE: flat model fits with chi2=0; any non-flat model has chi2>0. Ratio is infinity.

gamma_scaling.note: No valid Gamma measurements: R2=-0.217 at all beta points (negative R2 means exponential decay model is worse than flat mean). The envelope is not decaying exponentially in the t=[3,6] window at any beta. Gamma cannot be extracted with the R2>0.3 quality gate.

hawking_page_dip.note: Peak amplitudes are identical across all beta. No non-monotonic behavior.

truncation_error.note: Zero truncation error because exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs> = C*|psi_gs> analytically. Both step counts give the same result.

root_cause_analysis.diagnosis: The single-copy imaginary-time protocol is provably unable to construct a thermal state when initialized from an energy eigenstate.
root_cause_analysis.mathematical_proof: exp(-beta*H/2)|E_n> = exp(-beta*E_n/2)|E_n>. For psi_gs = |E_0>, the thermal state is exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs>/norm = exp(-beta*E_gs/2)|psi_gs>/norm = |psi_gs>. The normalized state is IDENTICAL to the ground state for ALL finite beta. This is exact, not approximate.
root_cause_analysis.verified_numerically: Overlap |<psi_gs|psi_beta>| = 1.000000000 confirmed at beta=1, 5, 20, 100 (limited to float64 precision).
root_cause_analysis.beta_range_vs_crossover: Even beta=1 satisfies beta*Delta_E = 0.125 >> 0, so the ground state dominates exp(-beta*H). The single-copy protocol would only reveal thermal mixing if initialized in a superposition of energy eigenstates (e.g., from a finite-T DMRG or imaginary-time TEBD starting from a high-T product state).
what_a_real_thermal_state_requires: Mixed state: rho(beta) = exp(-beta*H)/Z  -- requires density matrix, not pure statevector
Thermofield double: |TFD> = (1/sqrt(Z)) * sum_n exp(-beta*E_n/2)|n>_L|n>_R  -- doubles register to 2L qubits
Imaginary-time TEBD from infinite-T product state |+>^L -- correct but requires bond dimension chi
Matrix product thermal state (MPTS) at finite chi
root_cause_analysis.protocol_verdict: The mandatory constraint in HYP-024 feasibility_notes specified this protocol (exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs>) as a solution to TFD memory cost. This was an error in the feasibility analysis: the protocol does not produce a thermal state when applied to an energy eigenstate. The TFD cost concern was valid; the proposed workaround was not.

results.conclusion_paragraph: HYP-2026-024 tests whether the MERA boundary transport time T(beta) follows the Wang-He BTZ horizon-absorption curve when the boundary state is thermalized. Gate 1 (self-consistency) PASSED exactly: T(beta=100) = 2.2500, reproducing HYP-006's baseline at 0.00% residual. The pre-committed operator is Delta=1 (energy primary epsilon), giving predicted Gamma(beta) = 2*pi/beta, locked before any fitting. The N=16 beta ladder spanning {100, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1} -- two orders of magnitude in temperature -- yielded T(beta) = 2.2500 at every single point, varying 0.00% across the ladder. This triggers refutation criterion (b): T(beta) is flat within error, contradicting the predicted monotonic decrease toward the BTZ horizon. The root cause is proven analytically: exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs> normalizes to |psi_gs> for any beta when initialized from an energy eigenstate, so the protocol constructs the ground state at every temperature and the transport outcome is necessarily beta-independent. The truncation error bound is 0.000% (both n_steps=20 and n_steps=40 give identical results for the same reason). Gamma(beta) is untestable (R2 < 0 for all beta, envelope not decaying). VERDICT: REFUTED via criterion (b). CRITICAL CAVEAT: this refutes the testability of the protocol, NOT necessarily the Wang-He physics. The underlying BTZ prediction may be correct; a thermofield-double or imaginary-time TEBD from a product-state initial condition would be required to test it. The feasibility analysis in HYP-2026-024 contained an error: it proposed the single-copy imaginary-time protocol as a workaround for TFD memory cost, but this workaround does not produce a thermal state.

classical_baseline.transport_method: HYP-006 protocol: Gaussian Y-perturbation, expm_multiply time evolution, envelope extraction
classical_baseline.hamiltonian: Wang-He Eq 1: L/(4*pi)*sum_j[X_{j-1}Z_jX_{j+1} - X_jX_{j+1}], PBC, identical to holographic_transport_16q.py

notes: SIM-2026-026 tests HYP-2026-024. The REFUTED verdict is criterion-driven and honest-broker: the protocol does not probe what the hypothesis claims it probes. The feasibility_notes error (single-copy imaginary-time as a thermal state) is documented explicitly. HYP-2026-024 should be updated to NEEDS_REFINEMENT with a note that the protocol must be replaced by thermofield-double or imaginary-time TEBD before the physics claim can be tested. Wang-He (2603.07639) BTZ physics is not refuted -- only the specific protocol proposed in HYP-024 is shown to be incapable of testing it at local statevector scale.
